title.rendered: Is Ice Spice coming to Fortnite? Leaks, skins, release date, and more

content.rendered:
Courtesy of recent leaks, there is growing anticipation around Ice Spice’s imminent arrival in Fortnite. The popular American rapper is expected to join as part of the second wave of Fortnite’s collaboration with the SpongeBob SquarePants IP, which is centered around 2025’s The SpongeBob Movie: Search for SquarePants.

Once this content update is officially confirmed, Ice Spice will become the fifth singer to be added to Fortnite in 2026. Previous additions this year have included her contemporaries such as Chappell Roan, Laufey, and Olivia Rodrigo.

Ice Spice Fortnite skin leaked

As shared by renowned leakers Shiina and HYPEX, Ice Spice looks set to land in Fortnite via a SpongeBob SquarePants promo. The leaks reveal an Ice Spice skin, an umbrella pickaxe, an emote inspired by her viral “Big Guy” song, and a back bling modeled around the character she voiced in the 2025 animated film. Moreover, all these items will also be available in the Ice Spice bundle.

REVEALED SPONGEBOB WAVE 2 SO FAR

Ice Spice still got a free instrument from Twitch Drops on July 23, Fortnite hasn't announced it yet but Twitch did pic.twitter.com/GCLqsDsWMk

— HYPEX (@HYPEX) July 20, 2026

At the time of writing, this collab hasn’t yet been announced or even teased by Fortnite. However, Shiina suggests that the confirmation could arrive as soon as July 22, ahead of this week’s Twitch Drops.

All SpongeBob cosmetics in Fortnite leaked so far

Apart from Ice Spice, the leaks thus far have revealed that the upcoming SpongeBob SquarePants partnership would also bring Patrick Star into the mix. More specifically, Patrick seems poised to be added as a sidekick, along with three different styles: cel-shaded, gradient, and pirate. Additionally, the beloved character is also set to get two different emotes.

ALL KNOWN SPONGEBOB COSMETICS & STYLES

Patrick seems to have 2x Sidekick Emotes pic.twitter.com/8ZLT0m3JdJ

— Shiina (@ShiinaBR) July 20, 2026

A few other SpongeBob SquarePants-related items that have also surfaced are the jellyfish back bling, the ice cream back bling, and the jellyfish net pickaxe. This takes the count of leaked content from the forthcoming Fortnite collab to ten, excluding bundles.

Wrapping up

Thanks to the popularity of SpongeBob and Ice Spice, along with the fact that the “Big Guy” song was a viral sensation last year, this collab has all the favorable conditions to turn out successful. Besides that, whether or not this team-up also leads to new in-game events or possibly new sprites is something only time will tell.

  • Fortnite teases Spider-Man Brand New Day collab
  • How to get MCU Iron Man and Captain America skins in Fortnite
  • How to get Stranger Things skins in Fortnite

mainEntity.name: Is there a lightweight alternative to Adobe Acrobat for Windows?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. All four tools tested here are built as smaller, faster alternatives to Acrobat. PDNob comes closest to matching Acrobat's editing depth while staying under 600MB installed, and PDF-XChange Editor covers most of Acrobat's day-to-day functions in a portable build with no installer at all.

mainEntity.name: Is a portable PDF editor safer or more private than an installed one?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, Photographic Styles are designed for still photos and do not affect video recordings. Portability and privacy are separate things. A portable app like PDF-XChange Editor Portable avoids leaving an installation footprint on a shared PC, but it still processes files locally the same way an installed editor does. For actual data privacy, a self-hosted option like Stirling-PDF is the stronger choice since files never leave your own server.

mainEntity.name: Is there an open-source lightweight PDF editor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Xournal++ and Stirling-PDF are both open-source in this test. Xournal++ is a lightweight desktop app built for annotation, while Stirling-PDF is a self-hosted, browser-based tool with 60+ PDF operations that keeps every file on your own hardware.

title.rendered: Fortnite teases Spider-Man Brand New Day collab

content.rendered:
Spider-Man is swinging into Fortnite soon, as confirmed by a new teaser posted via the game’s official social media handle. The latest collaboration with Marvel’s webhead is set to come on the heels of Spider-Man Brand New Day, scheduled to release on July 31, 2026.

Fortnite is a melting pot of trending collabs, so obviously it’s not surprising that the highly popular online title is doing another one ahead of a major pop culture event, which in this case is the launch of the fourth MCU Spider-Man film. Thanks to the recent tease, Spider-Man and Fortnite fans alike are noticeably excited for potential themed content dropping in the game, following weeks of constant rumors.

Fortnite shares glimpse of Spider-Man Brand New Day collab

On July 21, Fortnite officially acknowledged its forthcoming collab with Spider-Man Brand New Day, with a 20-second teaser video posted on X. It showed buildings in the Fortnite map covered with webs as well as a Brand New Day-inspired mural, as the iconic Spider-Man theme music played in the background. Notably, the mural has been available in the game since at least a week before this post.

These webs look kinda familar… 🤔🕸️ pic.twitter.com/LjOK6qU2uf

— Fortnite (@Fortnite) July 21, 2026

In the comments, Fortnite players have responded positively and shared their own wishlist of in-game items they want added as part of the collab. These range from a cell-shaded version of the Spider-Man outfit to Spider-Man’s Web Shooters, which originally appeared in Fortnite in December 2021 during Chapter 3 Season 1.

Fortnite x Spider-Man Brand New Day collab expected content

To some fans’ relief, Spider-Man Mythic items, including Spider-Man’s Web Shooters, have been reported to be part of the new update by popular leaker HYPEX. Besides that, previous leaks have also talked about a Spider-Man Sprite being added to Fortnite, which would fall in line with how Batman also got a sprite version when the ongoing Hot Bat Summer promotion launched.

SPIDERMAN MYTHICS RETURN TO FORTNITE NEXT UPDATE pic.twitter.com/V19b7iPOmj

— HYPEX (@HYPEX) July 21, 2026

Moreover, a new Spider-Man outfit inspired by the superhero’s look in Spider-Man Brand New Day is among the most expected additions. There is also a Punisher Set, consisting of the titular anti-hero’s skin and other gear, rumored to be added to the game. Other skins that have surfaced online include ones based on Tom Holland’s Peter Parker and Zendaya’s MJ.

Final thoughts

Marvel has long been a key collaborator of Fortnite, even getting two entire seasons (Chapter 2 Season 4 aka “The Nexus War” and Chapter 5 Season 4 aka “Absolute Doom”) dedicated to its superheroes and supervillains. So, it’s natural that fans are thrilled to see another partnership between the two media behemoths.

The rumored new skins and returning Mythic items are undoubtedly exhilarating. However, I’m more interested in seeing how Spider-Man carves its own niche among other sprites, if the rumors of the arachnid-like hero getting its own sprite turn out to be true. Anyway, that looks like something we will hopefully learn more about very soon.

You may also enjoy:

  • How to get MCU Iron Man and Captain America skins in Fortnite
  • How to get Stranger Things skins in Fortnite
  • How to get the Lionel Messi skin in Fortnite

mainEntity.name: Is there a lightweight alternative to Adobe Acrobat for Windows?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. All four tools tested here are built as smaller, faster alternatives to Acrobat. PDNob comes closest to matching Acrobat's editing depth while staying under 600MB installed, and PDF-XChange Editor covers most of Acrobat's day-to-day functions in a portable build with no installer at all.

mainEntity.name: Is a portable PDF editor safer or more private than an installed one?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, Photographic Styles are designed for still photos and do not affect video recordings. Portability and privacy are separate things. A portable app like PDF-XChange Editor Portable avoids leaving an installation footprint on a shared PC, but it still processes files locally the same way an installed editor does. For actual data privacy, a self-hosted option like Stirling-PDF is the stronger choice since files never leave your own server.

mainEntity.name: Is there an open-source lightweight PDF editor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Xournal++ and Stirling-PDF are both open-source in this test. Xournal++ is a lightweight desktop app built for annotation, while Stirling-PDF is a self-hosted, browser-based tool with 60+ PDF operations that keeps every file on your own hardware.

content.rendered:
Buying premium earbuds has become surprisingly difficult. Every new launch promises smarter AI, stronger noise cancellation, and “studio-quality” sound. However, after carefully considering the features of the latest Apple AirPods Pro 3 and Samsung Galaxy Buds 4 Pro, I realized that the best earbuds aren’t necessarily the ones with the longest feature list.

If you’re deciding between these two earbuds, this guide will help you find an answer. I’ll compare AirPods Pro 3 vs Galaxy Buds 4 Pro based on sound quality, ANC, comfort, battery life, call performance, AI features, ecosystem advantages, and long-term value. So, you can choose the right pair.

AirPods Pro 3 vs Galaxy Buds 4 Pro: Quick spec comparison

AirPods Pro 3 vs Galaxy Buds 4 Pro: What differences I felt

Sound quality: Samsung sounds more exciting

If sound quality is your top priority, this is the closest battle between the two. Both earbuds deliver flagship-level audio, but they have very different personalities.

AirPods Pro 3 focus on balance and accuracy. Apple has upgraded to a new multiport acoustic architecture that improves airflow for deeper bass, a wider soundstage, and clearer vocals. A custom high-excursion driver and high dynamic range amplifier, powered by the H2 chip, produce detailed sound with exceptionally low distortion.

The best part is features like Adaptive EQ automatically tune audio based on how the earbuds fit your ears, while Personalized Spatial Audio with dynamic head tracking creates a more immersive listening experience. I really enjoy its lossless audio on my iPhone 17. Also, the upcoming custom EQ features on iOS 27 will be a game changer.

Samsung, however, packs considerably more hardware into the Galaxy Buds 4 Pro. Each earbud features an 11mm Super Wide Woofer for powerful low frequencies and a 5.5mm Planar Tweeter for crisp, detailed highs. Moreover, the independent dual amplifiers help reduce distortion while keeping bass, mids, and treble clean and well-defined.

I also felt the Buds 4 Pro extract more audio detail thanks to 24-bit/96kHz Hi-Res Audio and Samsung Seamless Codec (SSC UHQ). The music sounds deeper, with punchier bass and finer treble. The separation between bass, mids, and highs is particularly impressive.

Additionally, Samsung includes Adapt Sound, 360 Audio with Head Tracking, and a customizable 9-band EQ, giving users much more control over their listening experience. The Bluetooth LE audio and Auracast give stability.

For daily usage, the choice becomes a matter of personal preferences. The AirPods Pro 3 serve me perfectly in all cases, from podcasts, music and movies to calls. Galaxy Buds 4 Pro, on the other hand, is my buddy for listening to pop, EDM, hip-hop, and action movies. It sounds more lively with stronger bass and brighter treble.

Winner: Galaxy Buds 4 Pro

Also read: I replaced my AirPods Pro 3 with Sony WF-1000XM6: The difference shocked me

Noise Cancellation: Apple still sets the benchmark

Active Noise Cancellation (ANC) is one of the biggest reasons people spend over $200 on premium earbuds, and both Apple and Samsung have made significant improvements.

AirPods Pro 3 use Apple’s H2 chip to power Active Noise Cancellation, which intelligently reduces unwanted sounds before they reach your ears. Apple says the earbuds continuously process environmental noise in real time to adapt the level of noise cancellation. Also, I feel the fitted eartip seal contributes to passive noise isolation.

Samsung counters with Adaptive Noise Control on the Galaxy Buds 4 Pro. Using multiple microphones and Galaxy AI, the earbuds continuously analyze your environment and adjust the level of noise cancellation automatically.

I tested both when commuting, working in a busy café, and flying, and they did an excellent job of reducing low-frequency noises like airplane engines, train rumbles, air conditioners, and office chatter. But whenever I am outside or in a noisy place, my first choice is always AirPods.

Winner: AirPods Pro 3

Transparency Mode: Apple is still in a league of its own

Transparency mode has evolved from a nice-to-have feature into something you’ll likely use every day. Whether you’re ordering coffee, chatting with a coworker, or listening for train announcements, a great transparency mode lets you stay aware of your surroundings without taking your earbuds out.

AirPods Pro 3 continue to set the standard. Apple uses the H2 chip and computational audio to make outside sounds feel remarkably natural. Instead of simply amplifying ambient noise, the earbuds process it in real time, so voices sound clear and environmental sounds remain balanced.

I also really like Adaptive Audio, which intelligently blends Active Noise Cancellation and Transparency mode based on your surroundings, while Conversation Awareness automatically lowers your media volume and enhances nearby voices when you begin speaking.

Samsung has made major improvements with the Galaxy Buds 4 Pro. Its Adaptive Ambient Sound uses AI to analyze your environment and lets important sounds pass through naturally. Also, Voice Detect successfully recognized when I’m speaking and lowered the media volume. Thus, conversations feel more natural without manually switching modes.

Both earbuds allow you to be fully aware of the surrounding sounds easily, but Apple does it in a more sophisticated way. Voices sound more lifelike, background noise is processed more naturally, and the automatic transitions between listening and talking happen so smoothly that you rarely think about the technology working in the background.

Winner: AirPods Pro 3

Comfort and fit: Both are comfortable, but they feel very different

Comfort is one of the most personal aspects of any pair of earbuds. Even the best sound quality won’t matter if your earbuds become uncomfortable after an hour. Fortunately, both the AirPods Pro 3 and Galaxy Buds 4 Pro are designed for extended listening sessions, but they take different approaches to fit.

AirPods Pro 3 retain Apple’s lightweight, stem-style design with four sizes of silicone ear tips to help users find a secure seal. The earbuds are compact, distribute their weight evenly, and sit comfortably in the ear. I recommend taking the Ear Tip Fit Test on your iPhone to check if you’re using the right ear tips for the best comfort, sound quality, and Active Noise Cancellation.

Samsung redesigned the Galaxy Buds 4 Pro with a more ergonomic shape and softer ear tips for a relaxed fit. Like Apple’s earbuds, Samsung includes multiple silicone ear tip sizes to help users achieve a proper seal. The lightweight design and improved weight distribution make the Buds 4 Pro comfortable enough for long listening sessions.

Winner: Tie

Call quality: Clear voices on both, but Apple is more consistent

Premium earbuds are no longer just for listening to music—they’re also expected to handle video meetings, phone calls, and voice chats with ease. Thankfully, both the AirPods Pro 3 and Galaxy Buds 4 Pro deliver excellent call quality.

AirPods Pro 3 use beamforming microphones, an inward-facing microphone, and Apple’s H2 chip to isolate your voice while reducing background noise like traffic, wind, and office chatter. I always enable Voice Isolation to keep calls and meetings clear even in noisy environments.

Samsung takes a similarly advanced approach. The Galaxy Buds 4 Pro feature a 6-microphone system paired with a Voice Pickup Unit and Galaxy AI to separate your voice from surrounding noise. I liked its AI-powered Super Clear Call for better speech clarity, especially in outdoor environments with wind and background sounds.

Winner: AirPods Pro 3

Battery life: Samsung lasts longer

Battery life is another area where both earbuds perform well.

AirPods Pro 3 offer up to 8 hours of ANC-enabled and 10 hours with ANC listening time on a single charge, with the USB-C charging case extending total playback to around 24 hours. Apple also supports MagSafe, Qi wireless charging, and fast charging, giving you roughly two hours of listening from just a 20-minute charge in the case.

The Galaxy Buds 4 Pro provided up to 6 hours of playback with ANC enabled and up to 26 hours with the charging case. Turn ANC off, and the total battery life stretches even further. You can use USB-C and Qi wireless charging to get 85 minutes of listening time in 10 minutes. I even used the Galaxy Wearable app to check the detailed battery health and manage power-saving features.

Although the AirPods Pro 3 have a greater battery life, Samsung’s charging case delivers more total listening time, giving frequent travelers and heavy users a bit more flexibility.

Winner: Tie

AI features: Samsung packs more AI, Apple focuses on everyday utility

Artificial intelligence has quickly become one of the biggest differentiators between premium earbuds. While both the AirPods Pro 3 and Galaxy Buds 4 Pro leverage AI to enhance the user experience, they have very different priorities.

AirPods Pro 3 work closely with Apple Intelligence and offer additional features besides just playing music. For example, I depend on its Live Translation, which helps translate conversations in real time when paired with a compatible iPhone.

Apple also added FDA-cleared Hearing Aid support, allowing AirPods Pro 3 to function as an over-the-counter hearing aid for users with mild to moderate hearing loss. Combined with Conversation Awareness, Adaptive Audio, and Siri integration, the earbuds intelligently adjust audio based on your surroundings while making daily interactions feel effortless.

Samsung takes a more feature-rich approach with the Galaxy Buds 4 Pro. Powered by Galaxy AI, the earbuds support Interpreter, enabling real-time, face-to-face language translation directly through compatible Galaxy devices. I have set up Google Gemini as my assistant for AI-powered hands-free actions.

On top of that, features like Voice Detect, Adaptive Noise Control, and Adaptive EQ continuously optimize the listening experience without requiring manual adjustments.

Winner: Galaxy Buds 4 Pro

Apple vs Samsung ecosystem: Your smartphone decides the winner

On paper, the AirPods Pro 3 and Galaxy Buds 4 Pro look evenly matched. In reality, the experience you get depends almost entirely on the phone in your pocket.

If you own an iPhone, the AirPods Pro 3 feel like a natural extension of your Apple devices. Pairing takes just a tap, and the earbuds automatically switch between your iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Apple Watch without any manual setup. Features like Find My, Personalized Spatial Audio, Siri, etc., all work together to create an experience that’s effortless and consistent.

The Galaxy Buds 4 Pro offer a similar level of integration, but only within Samsung’s ecosystem. Pair them with a compatible Galaxy smartphone, and you unlock Galaxy AI, Hi-Res Audio, Auto Switch between Galaxy devices, Interpreter, 360 Audio, and SmartThings Find, and more. Moreover, the Galaxy Wearable app offers more customization like EQ controls and sound preferences.

Winner: Depends on your ecosystem

Which earbuds are better for different users?

There’s no one-size-fits-all answer. Here’s a quick recommendation based on how you plan to use your earbuds.

Buy AirPods Pro 3 if you:

  • Use an iPhone, iPad, Mac, or Apple Watch
  • Want the best Transparency Mode on the market
  • Prefer a balanced, natural sound signature
  • Make frequent FaceTime or voice calls
  • Want advanced health features like clinical-grade Hearing Test, Hearing Aid, built-in in-ear heart rate sensors, and active hearing protection
  • Want the smoothest overall user experience

Buy Galaxy Buds 4 Pro if you:

  • Own the latest Samsung Galaxy phone
  • Prefer deeper bass and a more energetic sound
  • Want 24-bit Hi-Res Audio and more audio customization
  • Need longer battery life with the charging case
  • Like AI-powered features such as Interpreter and Voice Detect
  • Want premium features at a competitive price

My Recommendation: If you’re buying premium earbuds, don’t chase the one with the longer feature list. Buy the one built for your ecosystem. An iPhone user will almost always have a better experience with AirPods Pro 3, while Galaxy users will get far more value from the Galaxy Buds 4 Pro.

Final verdict: Which premium earbuds should you buy?

After comparing the AirPods Pro 3 and Galaxy Buds 4 Pro across different parameters, one thing becomes obvious: both are among the best wireless earbuds you can buy, but they’re designed for different users.

The AirPods Pro 3 excel in the areas Apple has always prioritized: industry-leading Transparency Mode, excellent noise cancellation, outstanding call quality, and seamless integration across the Apple ecosystem. They deliver a polished, hassle-free experience that simply works.

The Galaxy Buds 4 Pro, meanwhile, impress with their 11mm Super Wide Woofer, 5.5mm Planar Tweeter, 24-bit Hi-Res Audio, stronger bass, longer overall battery life, and a growing suite of Galaxy AI features. They also offer more sound customization, making them the better choice for listeners who enjoy tweaking their audio.

Which earbuds caught your eye? Let me know in the comments below!

mainEntity.name: Is there a lightweight alternative to Adobe Acrobat for Windows?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. All four tools tested here are built as smaller, faster alternatives to Acrobat. PDNob comes closest to matching Acrobat's editing depth while staying under 600MB installed, and PDF-XChange Editor covers most of Acrobat's day-to-day functions in a portable build with no installer at all.

mainEntity.name: Is a portable PDF editor safer or more private than an installed one?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, Photographic Styles are designed for still photos and do not affect video recordings. Portability and privacy are separate things. A portable app like PDF-XChange Editor Portable avoids leaving an installation footprint on a shared PC, but it still processes files locally the same way an installed editor does. For actual data privacy, a self-hosted option like Stirling-PDF is the stronger choice since files never leave your own server.

mainEntity.name: Is there an open-source lightweight PDF editor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Xournal++ and Stirling-PDF are both open-source in this test. Xournal++ is a lightweight desktop app built for annotation, while Stirling-PDF is a self-hosted, browser-based tool with 60+ PDF operations that keeps every file on your own hardware.

title.rendered: How to get Vini Jr Sprite in Fortnite: All locations

content.rendered:
Fortnite has recently released a lot of in-game content to attract soccer fans. From the Striker Sprite to skins based on soccer stars such as Lionel Messi and David Beckham, there has been no shortage of variety. Now, the online game has turned another soccer sensation into a sprite by releasing the Vini Jr Sprite.

Standing out from the other sprites in Fortnite, the Vini Jr Sprite offers a distinct ability to inflict damage by sliding once you have sprinted for a short time. Moreover, slidekicking your enemies with this sprite equipped also boosts the rate of fire and reload speed.

This Mythic-tier sprite is available in just one variant and can only be obtained from chests, especially Sprite Chests. The following chest locations are particularly known to offer the Vini Jr Sprite.

Where to find Vini Jr Sprite in Fortnite

1. Golden Grove

Near the southern coast of Golden Grove, there is a platform with blue rails surrounded by a few rocks. There is a chest there that opens, which can give you the Vini Jr Sprite.

2. Calamari Canyon

In front of the big lake in Calamari Canyon, there is a lighthouse/tower. Enter it and go all the way to the top-most floor. There, you will find a chest that has a fair chance of spawning the Vini Jr Sprite.

3. Heatwave Harbor

Towards the south of Heatwave Harbor, there is an island to the left of the soccer pitch. Go to the southernmost edge of that island and head to the top of the cliff there. Upon reaching the peak, you will encounter a Sprite Chest from which players have collected the Vini Jr Sprite.

4. Frosted Flats

In Frosted Flats, near the western edge of the snowy area, there is an expansive blue building. Once you enter that, go past the closed door and descend into the basement, at the end of which you will find a vault. Inside it, you will find multiple chests and mythic weapons. Opening one of those chests is known to spawn highly rare sprites such as the Vini Jr one.

Other ways to get Vini Jr Sprite

Take it from an opponent

This is basically a life hack for Fortnite players. Instead of searching for ultra-rare sprites yourself, you can check for your opponents possibly carrying the same.

First off, as soon as you are in the pre-match lobby, go around and check the backs of each player to see if they have any sprite you may be interested in. In case you do spot one, memorize the outfit of that player and wait for him to jump off during the Battle Bus sequence. Next, chase down and eliminate him to obtain the desired sprite.

Borrow it from a friend

Throughout Chapter 7 Season 3, the Fortnite community has seen indexing emerge as a great way to fill their sprite collection. For this, you just need to find a player who already owns a sprite you want and then borrow and extract the same during a match, before returning it to the original owner. You can look for those willing to let you index the sprite in the “sprite-runners-network” channel within the game’s official Discord server.

Wrapping up

Thanks to the recently concluded FIFA World Cup, we have seen a bunch of different soccer-related collabs in Fortnite over the past month. From the Lionel Messi skin to the Vini Jr cosmetics, several different players have been the focal point of these content drops.

However, the Striker Sprite and the Vini Jr Sprite have arguably been the most impactful additions, as their role is not merely cosmetic but also affects the gameplay significantly. I, for one, have certainly been enjoying my time in Fortnite with these soccer-inspired sprites and can’t wait to continue using them in future matches.

FAQs

How many Vini Jr Sprite variants are there in Fortnite?

There is no other variant besides the base one for the Vini Jr Sprite.

How rare is the Vini Jr Sprite?

Vini Jr Sprite has Mythic rarity and hence is among the rarest sprites in Fortnite right now.

How many soccer-themed sprites are there in Fortnite?

There are two soccer-themed sprites in the game: Striker Sprite and Vini Jr Sprite.

  • How to get Batman Sprite in Fortnite
  • How to get galaxy sprites in Fortnite
  • How to get Gummy Zero Point Sprite in Fortnite

A portable app like PDF-XChange Editor Portable avoids leaving an installation footprint on a shared PC, but it still processes files locally the same way an installed editor does. For actual data privacy, a self-hosted option like Stirling-PDF is the stronger choice since files never leave your own server.

mainEntity.name: Is there an open-source lightweight PDF editor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Xournal++ and Stirling-PDF are both open-source in this test. Xournal++ is a lightweight desktop app built for annotation, while Stirling-PDF is a self-hosted, browser-based tool with 60+ PDF operations that keeps every file on your own hardware.

title.rendered: Apple took over a year to fix Hide My Email bug that exposed real email addresses

content.rendered:
Apple has fixed a vulnerability in Hide My Email that could expose a user’s real email address instead of keeping it anonymous. The company confirmed to 404 Media that the issue was fully patched in an update released on July 3.

The vulnerability affected Hide My Email, an iCloud+ feature that allows users to sign up for apps and websites without revealing their personal email address by using randomly generated aliases.

Spam-filtered emails could reveal users’ real email addresses

The vulnerability was first reported to Apple in June 2025 by EasyOptOuts co-founder Tyler Murphy.

According to Murphy, Apple acknowledged the report shortly after it was submitted and later informed him that the issue had been fixed in March 2026. However, after testing the feature again, Murphy discovered that the vulnerability was still present.

After additional discussions with Apple failed to produce a working fix, Murphy contacted 404 Media, which published a report detailing the issue earlier this month.

Now that Apple has released a patch, 404 Media has explained how the vulnerability worked.

If someone sent an email to a targeted Hide My Email alias and that message was automatically rejected as spam, the recipient’s real email address could appear in email server logs instead of remaining hidden behind the generated alias.

With the bug now fixed, 404 Media has explained how it worked. If someone sent an email to a targeted Hide My Email address and that message was automatically rejected as spam, the recipient’s real email address could appear in email server logs instead of remaining hidden.

According to Murphy and EasyOptOuts co-founder Ben Weiner, many users may never know whether they were affected because the rejected emails never reached their inbox or spam folder. Since those messages were filtered before delivery, users had no practical way to determine whether their real email address had been exposed.

“The bug has been fixed. However, we don’t think the risk to Hide My Email users has been eliminated.”

Murphy and Weiner argue that any Hide My Email alias created before July 7, 2026, should be considered potentially exposed, as mail transfer logs are often retained for extended periods.

In other words, while Apple’s update prevents the vulnerability from occurring in the future, any real email addresses already recorded in historical mail logs cannot be removed retroactively.

Apple is now facing a lawsuit over the vulnerability

The security flaw has also led to a proposed class-action lawsuit against Apple.

The plaintiffs allege that Apple violated California’s false advertising and consumer protection laws by continuing to market Hide My Email as a privacy feature despite allegedly being aware of the vulnerability before it was fully resolved.

The lawsuit is seeking class-action status and is expected to focus on whether Apple adequately protected users while the flaw remained unpatched.

Although Apple has now fixed the vulnerability, the legal case could determine whether the company responded appropriately after learning about the issue and whether users were sufficiently informed while the bug remained unresolved.

Does this vulnerability affect your confidence in Apple’s Hide My Email feature? Let us know in the comments below.

mainEntity.name: Is there a lightweight alternative to Adobe Acrobat for Windows?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. All four tools tested here are built as smaller, faster alternatives to Acrobat. PDNob comes closest to matching Acrobat's editing depth while staying under 600MB installed, and PDF-XChange Editor covers most of Acrobat's day-to-day functions in a portable build with no installer at all.

mainEntity.name: Is a portable PDF editor safer or more private than an installed one?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, Photographic Styles are designed for still photos and do not affect video recordings. Portability and privacy are separate things. A portable app like PDF-XChange Editor Portable avoids leaving an installation footprint on a shared PC, but it still processes files locally the same way an installed editor does. For actual data privacy, a self-hosted option like Stirling-PDF is the stronger choice since files never leave your own server.

mainEntity.name: Is there an open-source lightweight PDF editor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Xournal++ and Stirling-PDF are both open-source in this test. Xournal++ is a lightweight desktop app built for annotation, while Stirling-PDF is a self-hosted, browser-based tool with 60+ PDF operations that keeps every file on your own hardware.

title.rendered: Apple may launch a Klarna-backed device leasing program on July 28

content.rendered:
Apple is reportedly preparing a new way for U.S. customers to lease iPhones, iPads, Macs, and Apple Watches. The program, called Apple Upgrade, could launch on July 28 and replace two of the company’s existing iPhone payment options.

Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reports that Apple will offer the program online and at its U.S. retail stores, with Klarna providing the financial backing. Apple and Klarna have not announced the service, so its launch date and terms could still change.

How Apple Upgrade may work

Apple Upgrade would work more like a car lease than a standard installment purchase. Customers could upgrade before the term ends, pay off the device early, or choose to keep or return it at the end. Some of those choices may involve additional fees.

The reported terms vary by product:

A soft credit check would be required. Most models are expected to qualify, though the iPhone 16, entry-level iPad, Apple Watch SE, and MacBook Neo will reportedly be excluded. Business and education purchases would not be eligible either.

The biggest unanswered question is the total cost. Bloomberg says Apple plans to advertise lower monthly payments, but the report does not disclose interest rates, buyout prices, or a complete fee schedule. A smaller monthly bill does not necessarily mean a cheaper device once every payment and fee is counted.

Apple’s current iPhone upgrade plan may go away

Apple reportedly plans to stop accepting new customers for its iPhone Upgrade Program and standard iPhone financing after Apple Upgrade arrives.

The current Upgrade Program uses a 24-month installment loan, lets customers trade in and upgrade after making the equivalent of 12 payments, and bundles AppleCare+ into the monthly price. Apple Upgrade would cover more types of devices, but it would not include AppleCare. Buyers who want coverage would need to add it separately.

Apple has already moved away from handling some consumer credit itself. After ending Apple Pay Later in 2024, it began supporting installment plans from third-party providers, including Klarna, through Apple Pay.

Lower payments arrive after Apple raised hardware prices

The reported launch follows price increases across Apple’s Mac and iPad lineups in June. Apple blamed unusually high memory and storage costs, with some products becoming hundreds of dollars more expensive.

Leasing gives Apple a way to make those higher prices look more manageable month to month. Whether Apple Upgrade is a good deal will depend on the details Apple has not revealed yet: APR, early-upgrade fees, end-of-lease buyout costs, and what happens when a returned device is damaged.

If the reported July 28 launch happens, shoppers should compare the full amount payable with buying outright, Apple Card Monthly Installments, carrier financing, and trade-in offers. The monthly figure alone will not show which option costs less.

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. All four tools tested here are built as smaller, faster alternatives to Acrobat. mainEntity.name: Is a portable PDF editor safer or more private than an installed one?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, Photographic Styles are designed for still photos and do not affect video recordings. Portability and privacy are separate things. A portable app like PDF-XChange Editor Portable avoids leaving an installation footprint on a shared PC, but it still processes files locally the same way an installed editor does. title.rendered: Restrict vs. Block on Instagram: Everything you need to know

content.rendered:
Instagram offers several tools for managing unwanted interactions, but Restrict and Block are the two features people confuse most often. While both limit how someone can interact with your account, they serve very different purposes.

If you want to quietly manage someone’s comments and messages without them knowing, Restrict is the better choice. If you want to completely remove someone from your Instagram experience, Block is the way to go.

Keep reading to learn what happens when you restrict or block someone on Instagram, the key differences between the two, and when you should use each feature.

Instagram Restrict vs. Block: Quick comparison

What happens when you restrict someone on Instagram?

Instagram introduced Restrict as a more subtle alternative to blocking someone. Instead of cutting off contact entirely, it quietly limits how that person can interact with you.

When you restrict someone:

  • Their comments on your posts become visible only to them. If you want everyone else to see the comment, you’ll need to approve it manually.
  • New direct messages from the restricted account are sent to your Message Requests instead of your main inbox.
  • They can’t see when you’re active on Instagram or whether you’ve read their messages.
  • They can still view your profile, follow you, and interact with your public content.

One of the biggest advantages of Restrict is that Instagram doesn’t notify the other person. From their perspective, everything appears normal, even though their comments and messages are being quietly filtered.

When should you use Instagram Restrict?

Restrict is ideal when someone is becoming annoying or intrusive but hasn’t crossed the line into harassment.

For example, imagine a coworker comments on every post you share with sarcastic remarks. Blocking them could create unnecessary tension, especially if you work together. Restricting them allows you to hide those comments from everyone else without creating an awkward situation.

Similarly, if someone keeps sending messages that you don’t want to respond to, restricting them moves those messages out of your primary inbox while preventing them from knowing whether you’ve seen them.

What happens when you block someone on Instagram?

Blocking is Instagram’s strongest privacy feature. Once you block someone, they’re essentially removed from your Instagram experience.

A blocked user:

  • Can’t find your profile through Instagram Search.
  • Can’t view your posts, Stories, Reels, or Highlights.
  • Can’t send you messages.
  • Can’t like, comment on, or share your posts.
  • Can’t tag or mention you in posts or comments.

Instagram also lets you block the current account as well as any new accounts that person may create, making it much harder for them to contact you again.

Although your previous chat history remains in your inbox, the blocked person won’t be able to send any new messages unless you unblock them.

When should you block someone on Instagram?

Blocking is the right choice when you no longer want someone to have any access to your profile or content.

For instance, if an ex keeps trying to contact you, a stranger repeatedly sends inappropriate messages, or someone is harassing you through comments and DMs, blocking is the safest option.

If the behavior violates Instagram’s Community Standards, you should also consider reporting the account in addition to blocking it.

Instagram Restrict vs. Block: Which should you choose?

The right option depends entirely on what you’re trying to accomplish.

Choose Restrict if you want to reduce someone’s interactions without making it obvious. It’s ideal for classmates, coworkers, relatives, or anyone you don’t want to confront directly.

Choose Block if you want to completely stop someone from viewing your profile or contacting you. It’s the better option for dealing with harassment, fake accounts, spam, or people who repeatedly ignore your boundaries.

An easy way to remember the difference is:

  • Restrict quietly filters their interactions.
  • Block removes them from your Instagram experience altogether.

How to restrict someone on Instagram

Restricting someone only takes a few seconds.

  1. Head to the person’s Instagram profile you want to restrict.
  2. Tap the three-dot (More options) button in the top right corner.
  3. Select Restrict.

You can also restrict someone directly from the comments section by long-pressing their comment and choosing Restrict.

How to block someone on Instagram

If you decide blocking is the better option:

  1. Person’s Instagram profile → Three-dot button → Block.
  2. Tap the Block button to confirm.

Can someone tell if you restricted or blocked them on Instagram?

Instagram never notifies someone when you restrict or block them, but the two actions become noticeable in different ways.

Someone you’ve restricted may eventually realize something is different because their comments don’t receive replies, their messages stay in requests, and they can’t see your activity status. Even then, Instagram never explicitly tells them they’ve been restricted.

A blocked user will usually figure it out much faster because your profile disappears from search, they can’t open your account, and every interaction with your content stops working.

Summing up…

Both Restrict and Block are useful privacy tools, but they’re designed for different situations. Restrict quietly manages unwanted interactions without alerting the other person, while Block completely removes someone from your Instagram experience.

If you’re simply trying to avoid unwanted conversations or hide inappropriate comments, Restrict is usually enough. But if someone is harassing you, repeatedly contacting you, or making you feel unsafe, Block is the better option.

Still have questions about Instagram’s privacy features? Let us know in the comments below, and we’ll help you out.

mainEntity.name: Is there a lightweight alternative to Adobe Acrobat for Windows?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. All four tools tested here are built as smaller, faster alternatives to Acrobat. PDNob comes closest to matching Acrobat's editing depth while staying under 600MB installed, and PDF-XChange Editor covers most of Acrobat's day-to-day functions in a portable build with no installer at all.

mainEntity.name: Is a portable PDF editor safer or more private than an installed one?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, Photographic Styles are designed for still photos and do not affect video recordings. Portability and privacy are separate things. A portable app like PDF-XChange Editor Portable avoids leaving an installation footprint on a shared PC, but it still processes files locally the same way an installed editor does. For actual data privacy, a self-hosted option like Stirling-PDF is the stronger choice since files never leave your own server.

mainEntity.name: Is there an open-source lightweight PDF editor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Xournal++ and Stirling-PDF are both open-source in this test. Xournal++ is a lightweight desktop app built for annotation, while Stirling-PDF is a self-hosted, browser-based tool with 60+ PDF operations that keeps every file on your own hardware.

aioseo_head_json.author_bio:
Vikhyat has a bachelor’s degree in Electronic and Communication Engineering and over five years of writing experience. His passion for technology and Apple products led him to the tech writing space, where he specializes in writing App features, How-to guides, and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple users. 

 

About Vikhyat Rishi

  • Vikhyat has over five years of experience writing consumer tech content.
  • During his association with Smartprix and Beebom, Vikhyat has tested, tested, and reviewed numerous gadgets, including but not limited to smartphones, TVs, and more.
  • His passion for technology and Apple products led him to iGeeksBlog, where he specializes in writing How-to and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple enthusiasts.

Experience

Vikhyat embarked on his journey in consumer technology writing in 2019, driven by his passion for technology. He has sharpened his skills through associations with Smartprix and Beebom, where he extensively tested and reviewed various gadgets, focusing mainly on smartphones. Currently, Vikhyat specializes in crafting How-to and troubleshooting guides for the Apple ecosystem at iGeeksBlog. When not typing away on his MacBook Air, he loves exploring the real world.

title.rendered: Claude Code now supports Apple’s iOS simulator on Mac

content.rendered:
Anthropic has announced a new update for Claude Code on macOS that adds built-in support for Apple’s iOS simulator. The integration is available in public beta and lets developers build, test, and debug iPhone apps without leaving Claude Code.

The feature requires Xcode with the iOS platform installed and is available only in local Claude Code sessions on macOS.

Claude Code on desktop now works with the iOS simulator.

Build and run your iOS app, and the simulator opens in a panel right next to your conversation. Available today in public beta. pic.twitter.com/su4IguzPVb

— ClaudeDevs (@ClaudeDevs) July 21, 2026

Claude Code now works directly with the iOS Simulator

With the new simulator pane, Claude Code can automatically launch an app in the iOS Simulator when asked to build, run, or test a project. It can watch the app as it runs, interact with the interface, identify issues, apply fixes, and repeat the process until the task is complete.

Developers can keep using the iOS Simulator while Claude works in the background, so both can interact with the same app during development.

Unlike Anthropic’s Computer Use feature, the new integration communicates directly with the iOS Simulator instead of controlling the Mac like a human user. As a result, it doesn’t require macOS Accessibility or Screen Recording permissions.

Anthropic warns developers against using personal accounts

Anthropic says screenshots captured from the iOS Simulator are sent to its servers and stored under the company’s standard conversation retention policy. For that reason, Anthropic recommends avoiding personal or production accounts while Claude is interacting with the simulator.

The iOS Simulator integration is currently available in the public beta version of Claude Code for macOS. Anthropic has also published setup documentation for developers who want to try the feature.

Would you use Claude Code to build and test iPhone apps, or do you prefer working directly in Xcode? Let us know in the comments below.

mainEntity.name: Is there a lightweight alternative to Adobe Acrobat for Windows?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. All four tools tested here are built as smaller, faster alternatives to Acrobat. PDNob comes closest to matching Acrobat's editing depth while staying under 600MB installed, and PDF-XChange Editor covers most of Acrobat's day-to-day functions in a portable build with no installer at all.

mainEntity.name: Is a portable PDF editor safer or more private than an installed one?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, Photographic Styles are designed for still photos and do not affect video recordings. Portability and privacy are separate things. A portable app like PDF-XChange Editor Portable avoids leaving an installation footprint on a shared PC, but it still processes files locally the same way an installed editor does. For actual data privacy, a self-hosted option like Stirling-PDF is the stronger choice since files never leave your own server.

mainEntity.name: Is there an open-source lightweight PDF editor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Xournal++ and Stirling-PDF are both open-source in this test. Xournal++ is a lightweight desktop app built for annotation, while Stirling-PDF is a self-hosted, browser-based tool with 60+ PDF operations that keeps every file on your own hardware.

Vikhyat has a bachelor’s degree in Electronic and Communication Engineering and over five years of writing experience. His passion for technology and Apple products led him to the tech writing space, where he specializes in writing App features, How-to guides, and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple users. 

 

About Vikhyat Rishi

  • Vikhyat has over five years of experience writing consumer tech content.
  • During his association with Smartprix and Beebom, Vikhyat has tested, tested, and reviewed numerous gadgets, including but not limited to smartphones, TVs, and more.
  • His passion for technology and Apple products led him to iGeeksBlog, where he specializes in writing How-to and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple enthusiasts.

Experience

Vikhyat embarked on his journey in consumer technology writing in 2019, driven by his passion for technology. He has sharpened his skills through associations with Smartprix and Beebom, where he extensively tested and reviewed various gadgets, focusing mainly on smartphones. Currently, Vikhyat specializes in crafting How-to and troubleshooting guides for the Apple ecosystem at iGeeksBlog. When not typing away on his MacBook Air, he loves exploring the real world.

title.rendered: Today’s Apps Gone Free on The App Store

content.rendered:
Apps Free Gone deals are the best way to grab premium iPhone and iPad apps without paying anything. Developers frequently turn their paid apps free for a limited time, and we track these offers daily so you can enjoy powerful tools, premium features, and fun games completely free.

Bookmark this page to stay updated and never miss out.

Crestwall 4k Wallpapers

CrestWall 4K Wallpapers App is Now Available on the App Store.

We’re excited to announce that CrestWall 4K Wallpapers, developed by the team at iGeeksBlog, is now available on the App Store.

CrestWall brings a growing collection of hand-picked 4K wallpapers designed to make your iPhone look its best. Fro m stunning Depth Effect wallpapers to fresh weekly additions and carefully curated collections, every wallpaper is selected with quality and style in mind.

If you’ve enjoyed our content over the years, downloading CrestWall is a great way to support our work. We’d love for you to try it out and share your feedback.

CrestWall - 4K Wallpapers
Price: Free+

Today’s Apps Gone Free

Below you’ll find our hand-picked, regularly updated list of paid iOS apps and games that have gone free today.

ASABlocker
Price: Free

Authenticator App Vault+
Price: Free+

Markdown.md - Reader & Editor
Price: Free+

VRAMFit: LLM Calculator
Price: Free+

Offline AI Chat: Maivii AI
Price: Free+

Today’s Apps on SALE


Learn Spanish Through English
Price: $2.99

Trail Explorer: Cozy Adventure
Price: $0.99

ProCam MK II - Pro Camera
Price: $9.99

Aim990 Plus
Price: $5.99

WiFi Aid
Price: $5.99

How to Claim Free App Offers

Some free promotions require extra steps to unlock the deal. Here are tips to ensure you get the app for free:

  1. Download the app from the App Store.
  2. Open the app and complete any onboarding or sign-up process.
  3. Look for a “Free,” “Trial,” or “Lifetime” option make sure the price is $0 before confirming.
  4. For offers involving free trials, set a reminder to cancel before the trial ends to avoid being charged.

Always double-check the price at checkout. If you see a charge, the offer may have expired.

How to Manage or Cancel App Subscriptions on iOS

If you’ve started a free trial, it’s important to stay in control of your subscriptions. Learn how to manage or cancel App Store subscriptions before renewal to avoid unexpected charges.

  1. Open the Settings app on your iPhone or iPad.
  2. Tap your name at the top, then select Subscriptions.
  3. Find the app’s subscription and tap it.
  4. Tap Cancel Subscription (or Cancel Free Trial).
Note Canceling a free trial usually lets you keep using the app’s premium features until the trial ends.

Avoiding Common Free Trial Pitfalls

  1. Some trials convert to annual subscriptions by default—double-check the renewal terms.
  2. Trial periods can be as short as three days.
  3. Cancel at least 24 hours before the trial ends to avoid being charged (per App Store policy).
  4. Keep a simple list, or use a subscription tracker app if you claim multiple trials.

Why Do Apps Go Free?

Developers make their paid apps free temporarily for several reasons—all of which benefit you:

  • Boosting Visibility: Free promotions help apps climb the App Store charts, so you discover new and trending apps you might otherwise miss.
  • Attracting New Users: By offering premium apps for free, developers reach a wider audience, and you get to try top-quality apps risk-free.
  • Gathering Reviews: Free downloads often lead to more ratings and reviews, so you can find well-reviewed, trustworthy apps.
  • Standing Out from Competitors: To compete in a crowded market, developers offer exclusive free deals giving you access to apps that might usually be out of reach.
Example A note-taking app might go free for a day to gain users and reviews. You get organizational tools that normally cost $5—at no cost!

Why We Update Daily

App Store promotions can last just a few hours or up to a couple of days—so timing is everything. We update this list every day to ensure you:

  • Get the newest deals as soon as they’re available.
  • Never miss out on short-lived offers.
  • Maximize your savings—downloading just a few free apps each week could save you hundreds of dollars a year!

Developers: Get Your App Featured

Are you making your app free for a limited time?

Contact us or reach out on X (@iGeeksBlog) or Instagram (@iGeeksBlog) to get your app listed here. We’re happy to help more users discover your work!

Disclaimer: All apps are free at the time of publication. Prices and availability can change without notice. We are not responsible for any price changes or charges incurred.

Enjoy exploring new apps and unlocking premium features every day—without spending a cent! Don’t forget to bookmark this page and check back for the latest deals.

FAQs

How often do free app promotions change?

Promotions can change multiple times a day. Check this page daily to catch the latest deals before they expire.

Can I get a refund if I already bought an app that is now free?

No, previous purchases are not refunded if the app is later free. However, you’ll continue to receive updates and new features.

Are there hidden costs with free apps?

Some free apps may include In-app purchases (buying extra features or content), Subscription trials (which may auto-renew if not canceled), and Ads (to support the developer). Always read the app description and reviews before downloading.

How can I avoid accidental charges?

For trial-based offers, set a calendar reminder to cancel before the trial ends. Always make sure the price shows as $0 before confirming any purchase.

mainEntity.name: Is there a lightweight alternative to Adobe Acrobat for Windows?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. All four tools tested here are built as smaller, faster alternatives to Acrobat. PDNob comes closest to matching Acrobat's editing depth while staying under 600MB installed, and PDF-XChange Editor covers most of Acrobat's day-to-day functions in a portable build with no installer at all.

mainEntity.name: Is a portable PDF editor safer or more private than an installed one?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, Photographic Styles are designed for still photos and do not affect video recordings. Portability and privacy are separate things. A portable app like PDF-XChange Editor Portable avoids leaving an installation footprint on a shared PC, but it still processes files locally the same way an installed editor does. For actual data privacy, a self-hosted option like Stirling-PDF is the stronger choice since files never leave your own server.

mainEntity.name: Is there an open-source lightweight PDF editor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Xournal++ and Stirling-PDF are both open-source in this test. Xournal++ is a lightweight desktop app built for annotation, while Stirling-PDF is a self-hosted, browser-based tool with 60+ PDF operations that keeps every file on your own hardware.

aioseo_head_json.author_bio:
"The founder of iGeeksBlog, Dhvanesh, is an Apple aficionado, who cannot stand even a slight innuendo about Apple products. He dons the cap of editor-in-chief to make sure that articles match the quality standard before they are published."

About Dhvanesh

Ever since teenage years, gadgets and technology have held a special place in Dhvanesh's heart. This fascination with gadgets and their inner workings fueled a lifelong passion for exploration and troubleshooting. Disassembled electronic items scattered around the house became a familiar sight during his younger years, a testament to this insatiable curiosity.

From SEO Expert to Apple Evangelist

After completing his IT engineering diploma, Dhvanesh's professional journey began with a 4.5-year stint as an SEO executive, honing valuable digital marketing skills. However, the desire to share tech knowledge and connect with a like-minded community proved stronger. In 2012, Dhvanesh embarked on a new adventure, founding iGeeksBlog. This blog became a haven for Apple enthusiasts and tech aficionados seeking insightful and in-depth information about everything Apple.

A Decade of iGeeksBlog: Leading the Apple Charge

In the past 12 years, Dhvanesh has donned multiple hats at iGeeksBlog. As the founder, he has steered the blog’s vision, ensuring it remains a trusted resource for Apple users worldwide. Additionally, he has been serving as the CEO of iGeeks Media Private Limited for the past 4 years, overseeing the company's growth and development.

Beyond Writing: A Multifaceted Approach

Dhvanesh isn't just a prolific writer, having penned hundreds of articles for iGeeksBlog. He has also served as the blog’s Editor-in-Chief and Content Strategist, ensuring a consistent flow of high-quality content that caters to the diverse needs of the Apple user base. The passion for exploration extends beyond the written word. He has created numerous YouTube videos for iGeeksBlog, providing visual demonstrations and engaging directly with the audience.

Staying Connected with the Apple Ecosystem

Dhvanesh's dedication to the Apple community goes a step further. Currently, he also manages the iGeeksBlog+ weekly newsletter, delivering curated Apple news, gadgets, apps, tips and tricks straight to subscribers' inboxes. This unwavering commitment to Apple technology and a genuine desire to empower fellow users make him a valuable asset to the iGeeksBlog team.

title.rendered: ChatGPT Plus vs. Claude Pro: Which $20 subscription actually earns its keep?

content.rendered:
Both ChatGPT Plus and Claude Pro cost $20 a month, and both can make you a faster writer, researcher, developer, or student than their free tiers. The difference is that they aren’t trying to solve the same problem. ChatGPT Plus aims to be an all-in-one AI toolkit for writing, coding, research, images, voice, spreadsheets, and automation. Claude Pro focuses on delivering a more thoughtful conversation, stronger writing, and better instruction-following.

If I had to cancel one today, I’d keep ChatGPT Plus. It simply offers more value for the same price. But that doesn’t automatically make it the better choice for everyone. Depending on how you use AI, Claude Pro may still be the subscription that’s worth paying for.

ChatGPT Plus vs. Claude Pro: Quick comparison

(US web pricing before tax; App Store and regional pricing may vary.)

ChatGPT Plus vs. Claude Pro: Key differences

The biggest difference comes down to how each platform expects you to work. Claude is at its best in discussion. You’re shaping an idea, refining a plan, and going back and forth. Its tone stays consistent, it follows nuance across a long thread, and it rarely needs to be reminded of what you already told it.

ChatGPT Plus is built for throughput. Research, images, voice, spreadsheets, and code all sit in the same subscription, and the limits are loose enough that a big project rarely grinds to a halt.

The catch is that Claude’s biggest strength is also its biggest liability. Long conversations, big attachments, Research, Artifacts, and Claude Code all draw from the same allowance, and it empties faster than you’d expect. ChatGPT is easier to lean on for hours at a stretch, though you’ll occasionally get an answer that reads a little flatter and more over-structured than what Claude would have written.

What do you get with ChatGPT Plus and Claude Pro?

  • ChatGPT Plus gets you GPT-5.6 Sol, plus voice, native image generation, file and data analysis, Deep Research, Projects, custom GPTs, and Codex, which itself includes Sol, Terra, and Luna. More importantly, the limits are way more generous than Claude. You get like a 160-message limit per three hours on ChatGPT. Codex and ChatGPT work usage limits are also way higher than what Claude offers.
  • Claude Pro gets you Sonnet 5, Claude Code, Projects, Research, extended thinking, and connectors. It costs either $20/month or $200/year, which knocks the effective monthly price down to about $17. The one wrinkle is that Fable 5 isn’t part of the standard Pro allowance. It draws from a separate credit pool, and full included access sits behind a higher tier.

Model access is arguably the biggest difference between the two subscriptions. ChatGPT Plus hands you the best model and best limits. Whereas Claude does not provide you with Fable 5 in the Pro plan and also hits its limits way more than ChatGPT, so you have to stop your work for a few hours until your 5-hour limit resets again.

Claude still feels better to actually talk to

This remains Claude’s biggest strength. It can take a half-formed idea and work with it instead of flattening it into a bulleted list, and it’s noticeably better at preserving your voice when editing a long draft rather than rewriting over it. Switching from ChatGPT to Claude for long-form writing consistently cuts down the cleanup work afterward. That’s not a small thing if writing is most of what you do.

Artifacts round this out nicely: you can develop a document, chart, or small prototype alongside the conversation rather than as a separate export. Combined with Projects, connectors, and Skills, Claude’s website feels less like a chatbot and more like a workspace built around the conversation itself.

ChatGPT isn’t far behind on paper. It has Projects, custom GPTs, memory, and Tasks of its own. But when the work is really about thinking something through rather than producing a single final answer, Claude still has the edge.

Research and documents: it depends what comes next

Both tools can search the web, cite sources, read PDFs, and hold reference material inside a project. The real difference isn’t whether they can research—it’s what happens after the research is finished.

Claude is the stronger choice when the job is turning several long reports into one coherent argument. It carries a thread across long documents without the result feeling stitched together from parts. ChatGPT pulls ahead when the research is just the first step: it can inspect images, clean up a spreadsheet, run Python, generate charts, and reformat everything without leaving the conversation.

A practical rule of thumb is to reach for Claude when you’re comparing three long reports and need the stronger argument out the other side. Reach for ChatGPT when there’s also a messy CSV, some calculations, or multiple output formats involved. Either way, double-check the important claims, citations, and numbers yourself.

Images, voice, and data clearly favor ChatGPT

ChatGPT Plus can generate and edit social graphics, concept art, thumbnails, and mockups. Claude doesn’t compete in this category. It can analyze an image and build a visual Artifact from it, but it has no comparable image generator of its own.

Voice tells a similar story: ChatGPT’s voice mode is genuinely useful for hands-free brainstorming or camera-based questions, while Claude’s version is fine for conversation but not a reason to subscribe on its own. For anything involving numbers, such as running calculations, writing Python, explaining a CSV, or building a chart, ChatGPT handles mixed text, data, and visual work more comfortably than Claude does.

Coding is close. But ChatGPT is a no-brainer for the $20 Plan

In terms of coding quality, there’s very little separating them. Claude tends to write cleaner code, plan architecture more carefully, and nail the UI on a first attempt. ChatGPT, through Codex, is every bit as capable on hard engineering problems.

The bigger difference comes down to subscription value. Claude Pro includes Sonnet 5, with its newer model gated behind credits. ChatGPT Plus includes GPT-5.6 Sol and gives Codex access to three additional models. For a single $20 coding subscription, ChatGPT currently offers the broader model lineup and roomier limits.

The workflows differ too. Claude is more likely to question a weak assumption or suggest a cleaner approach while you’re still figuring out what to build, but it is also more likely to pause partway through a longer task. Codex, once a plan is approved, just executes: it edits files, verifies the result, and keeps going without much hand-holding.

In practice, that division of labor works well together. Use Claude to decide what to build and how it should work, then hand the approved plan to Codex to finish. Codex is also useful well outside of software, including writing from large folders, updating documents, and running repeatable reporting workflows, which makes ChatGPT Plus worth considering even if you’re not coding full-time.

However, as mentioned, Claude does not provide your Fable 5 in the Pro tier, and you will also hit your usage limits faster. So if you are not planning on buying additional credits on top of your Claude sub, then ChatGPT is a better option, as you get both the best model and better limits.

ChatGPT is the more reliable computer-use agent

Ask ChatGPT to investigate a system setting, dig through files, or complete a task in the browser, and it tends to find the right control and recover gracefully when something unexpected pops up. Claude can handle simple versions of the same workflow, but it’s more prone to losing track of a dialog box or picking the wrong control in a genuinely complex interface.

Neither should be trusted unsupervised around payments, account deletion, or sensitive files. But for routine work across a browser and desktop apps, ChatGPT is the safer bet today.

A couple of things to check before you subscribe

Both are consumer-tier plans, so read the data-handling terms before uploading client work, private code, or anything sensitive. Confidential company work needs a business plan, not a personal subscription. Neither $20 fee covers API usage: any app or automation built on an OpenAI or Anthropic API key is billed separately, and Claude may charge credits for usage beyond the standard Pro allowance.

Should you buy ChatGPT Plus or Claude Pro?

  • Most people: ChatGPT Plus. It covers more ground with fewer compromises.
  • Writers and editors: Claude Pro, if preserving your voice and cutting down on cleanup matters more than images, voice, or automation.
  • Researchers: Claude for synthesizing long documents into a single argument; ChatGPT when the work also involves spreadsheets, charts, or multiple output formats.
  • Developers: ChatGPT Plus for the strongest $20 coding-and-agent bundle; Claude if planning quality and collaborative problem-solving matter more to you than raw execution and limits.
  • Students: ChatGPT Plus for mixed coursework, research, and data work; Claude for essay-heavy or reading-intensive assignments.
  • Creators: ChatGPT Plus, since image generation, voice, research, and writing all live in one place.
  • Chat-first users: Claude Pro, if what you want is a genuinely good assistant to think alongside every day, and you’ll actually use Artifacts and Projects.
  • Occasional users: Neither, yet. Stick with the free tiers until a limit or a missing feature starts costing you real time.

For most people, I’d recommend subscribing to ChatGPT Plus and pairing it with Claude’s free plan. Upgrade to Claude Pro only when its stronger writing, planning, and Artifacts become essential parts of your daily workflow.

mainEntity.name: Is there a lightweight alternative to Adobe Acrobat for Windows?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. All four tools tested here are built as smaller, faster alternatives to Acrobat. PDNob comes closest to matching Acrobat's editing depth while staying under 600MB installed, and PDF-XChange Editor covers most of Acrobat's day-to-day functions in a portable build with no installer at all.

mainEntity.name: Is a portable PDF editor safer or more private than an installed one?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, Photographic Styles are designed for still photos and do not affect video recordings. Portability and privacy are separate things. A portable app like PDF-XChange Editor Portable avoids leaving an installation footprint on a shared PC, but it still processes files locally the same way an installed editor does. mainEntity.name: Is there a lightweight alternative to Adobe Acrobat for Windows?

title.rendered: Can you see mutual friends on Snapchat? Here’s what you can actually check

content.rendered:
Adding random people on Snapchat isn’t always a good idea. It’s usually better to connect with people you already know through school, work, family, or mutual friends. That’s where Snapchat’s mutual friends feature can help by giving you a little more confidence before sending a friend request.

Seeing that you share mutual friends with someone can make it easier to decide whether they’re actually someone you know or just another suggested profile.

Keep reading to learn how to check mutual friends on Snapchat, where to find these suggestions, and what the “mutual friends” label actually means.

Does Snapchat show mutual friends?

Yes, Snapchat lets you see when you have mutual friends with another user. On the Add Friends page, some suggested profiles display an “X mutual friends” label beneath the username, indicating how many friends you have in common.

The feature is more limited than many users expect. Snapchat only shows the number of mutual friends—it doesn’t reveal their names or profiles.

That can be frustrating if you have friends from different parts of your life, such as work, school, or family. Unless you already recognize the suggested profile, there’s no way to tell which shared friend connects you.

How to see mutual friends on Snapchat

You can check for mutual friends directly from Snapchat’s Add Friends page.

  1. Open Snapchat and tap the Add Friends icon in the top-right corner.
  2. Scroll through the suggested profiles until you find one with the “X mutual friends” label below the username.
  3. If you want to connect with that person, tap Add next to their profile.

Keep in mind that not every suggestion includes mutual friends. Snapchat may also recommend people based on your contacts, shared groups, or recently created accounts.

Related: What do Snapchat symbols mean? Every icon and emoji explained

Things to know before adding someone on Snapchat

Having mutual friends doesn’t automatically mean you know someone personally. Before sending a friend request, keep these tips in mind:

  • Don’t add someone just because they have mutual friends with you.
  • Make sure you actually recognize them.
  • Since Snapchat doesn’t reveal who your shared friends are, ask someone you know if you’re unsure about the person’s identity.
  • Allowing Snapchat access to your contacts can improve friend suggestions if you’re trying to find people you already know.
  • Avoid sending too many friend requests in a short period, especially to people you don’t know, as it could trigger spam protections.
  • If you don’t want Snapchat using your contacts for suggestions, you can revoke the Contacts permission from your phone’s settings.

Signing off…

That’s everything you need to know about Snapchat’s mutual friends feature. While the app doesn’t reveal who your mutual friends are, seeing the number of shared connections can still help you decide whether a suggested profile is worth adding.

Have a question about Snapchat’s mutual friends feature? Leave a comment below, and we’ll be happy to help.

mainEntity.name: Is there a lightweight alternative to Adobe Acrobat for Windows?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. All four tools tested here are built as smaller, faster alternatives to Acrobat. PDNob comes closest to matching Acrobat's editing depth while staying under 600MB installed, and PDF-XChange Editor covers most of Acrobat's day-to-day functions in a portable build with no installer at all.

mainEntity.name: Is a portable PDF editor safer or more private than an installed one?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, Photographic Styles are designed for still photos and do not affect video recordings. Portability and privacy are separate things. A portable app like PDF-XChange Editor Portable avoids leaving an installation footprint on a shared PC, but it still processes files locally the same way an installed editor does. For actual data privacy, a self-hosted option like Stirling-PDF is the stronger choice since files never leave your own server.

mainEntity.name: Is there an open-source lightweight PDF editor?

About Vikhyat Rishi

  • Vikhyat has over five years of experience writing consumer tech content.
  • During his association with Smartprix and Beebom, Vikhyat has tested, tested, and reviewed numerous gadgets, including but not limited to smartphones, TVs, and more.
  • His passion for technology and Apple products led him to iGeeksBlog, where he specializes in writing How-to and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple enthusiasts.

Experience
